items.prompt:
Some animals form groups that help members
A) survive
B) disappear
C) shrink
D) stop eating

steps: Groups can help animals find food and stay safe.

items.prompt:
Wolves hunt in a pack so they can
A) catch large prey together
B) sleep more
C) swim faster
D) fly

steps: A pack can catch prey one wolf could not.

items.prompt:
A herd of deer stays safer because
A) it has many eyes to watch for predators
B) it is louder
C) it is bigger food
D) it cannot move
items.answer: A) it has many eyes to watch for predators

items.prompt:
A tight school of fish helps the fish by
A) confusing predators
B) making them slower
C) attracting predators
D) doing nothing

steps: A swirling school makes it hard to target one fish.

items.prompt:
Why use evidence in an argument about groups?
A) To waste time
B) To show the group really helps members survive
C) To hide the truth
D) There is no reason
items.answer: B) To show the group really helps members survive

items.prompt:
Meerkats take turns watching for danger. This helps the group because
A) others can find food safely
B) it wastes energy
C) it attracts predators
D) it does nothing
items.answer: A) others can find food safely

steps: Taking turns watching keeps the group fed and safe.

items.prompt:
Which is the BEST evidence-based argument?
A) Groups never help animals
B) A wolf pack catches large prey one wolf cannot, so the group helps wolves survive
C) Wolves like company
D) Groups are fun
items.answer: B) A wolf pack catches large prey one wolf cannot, so the group helps wolves survive

steps: It uses evidence to show the group aids survival.

items.prompt:
A lone animal may be in more danger than one in a group because
A) it has fewer eyes to spot predators and no help getting food
B) it is always faster
C) groups are dangerous
D) being alone is always safer
items.answer: A) it has fewer eyes to spot predators and no help getting food

steps: A single animal lacks the group's shared watching and hunting.
